source_text: Propterea sicut per unum hominem in hunc mundum peccatum intravit et per peccatum mors et ita in omnes homines mors pertransiit, in quo omnes peccaverunt [n273] . Ad edomandam superbiam Iudaeorum, qui sibi necessariam pecca torum veniam non tantum quantum Gentilibus aestimabant, praerogativa legis sanctitatem suo generi vindicantes, in morbum humanae conversationis invadit et multitudinem delinquentium retro petit, ut quantum dominationis in hoc mundo iniquitas occupaverit, antiquitatis ipsius prodat auctoritas, quamque multa et veternosa crimina ab obscenitate praecedentium per manus mutuae imitationis posteris tradita Christi gratia sustulisset, ostenderet. Atque ob hoc recordationem facit primi hominis, non a quo peccatum coeperat, constat enim prius mulierem deliquisse, sed qui per privilegium sexus magisterium occupasset delicti: Per hunc ergo intravit peccatum et per peccatum mors, sine dubio illa quae peccatoribus id est aeterna promittitur, et ita - inquit - in omnes homines mors pertransiit, in quo omnes peccaverunt. Aperuit prorsus, qualiter haec mors transisset ad posteros, ob imitationem scilicet, non generationem.
pass_a_gloss: On this account as through one human being sin entered into this world and through sin death and so death passed through into all human beings, in whom all sinned. Toward taming the pride of the Jews, who were estimating a pardon of sins not so necessary for themselves as for the Gentiles, claiming holiness for their kind by a prerogative of the law, he invades the disease of human conversation and seeks backward the multitude of those offending, so that how much of domination iniquity has occupied in this world the authority of antiquity itself may betray, and how many and aged crimes handed down from the obscenity of those preceding through the hands of mutual imitation to posterity the grace of Christ had taken away, he would show. And on this account he makes a recollection of the first human being, not from whom sin had begun, for it stands that the woman first offended, but who through a privilege of sex had occupied the mastership of the offense: Through this one therefore sin entered and through sin death, without doubt that which is promised to sinners, that is eternal, and so, he says, death passed through into all human beings, in whom all sinned. He opened altogether how this death had passed to posterity, on account of imitation namely, not generation.

pass_b_english: ‘Therefore, just as through one man sin entered this world, and death through sin, and so death passed into all human beings, in whom all sinned’ (Romans 5:12). To tame the Jews’ pride—they thought they needed forgiveness of sins less than the Gentiles did, claiming holiness for their race through the law’s privilege—he attacks the disease of human conduct and traces the multitude of sinners backward. The authority of antiquity itself would thus reveal how great a dominion wickedness had seized in this world. He would show how many long-established crimes Christ’s grace had removed: crimes passed from the indecency of predecessors to descendants through the hands of mutual imitation. For this reason he recalls the first man, not as the one with whom sin began—it is established that the woman sinned first—but as the one who, through the privilege of his sex, had assumed leadership in wrongdoing. Through him, then, sin entered, and through sin death—undoubtedly the death foretold for sinners, namely eternal death. ‘And so,’ he says, ‘death passed into all human beings, in whom all sinned.’ He has made perfectly clear how this death passed to descendants: by imitation, not generation.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
